text:
rachel: Heads-up — company offsite in Austin next month. Quick question: should we encourage people to book a hotel near the venue or split into Airbnbs? pros/cons?
jason: Airbnb = cheaper for groups, kitchen + chill space. but noise + weird check-in times are real.
priya: Hotel wins for consistent wifi and breakfast. Also easier for late arrivals.
ben: +1 hotel. Also easier for reimbursement receipts and group rate.
amanda: Airbnb person here: we stayed together last year and it made dinners way simpler. but privacy for ppl who want quiet was an issue.
travis: logistics: if ppl share cars, parking at some downtown hotels is $$$. Airbnbs sometimes include free street parking but random.
rachel: good points. what about workspace? we need a couple of rooms for focused sessions and small breakouts.
jason: hotels usually have a meeting room we can book (even small boardrooms). cheaper than renting coworking for 4 hours.
priya: +1 on meeting room. also helpful for AV setup. hotels are used to this so hookups and tech are smoother.
amanda: Airbnb hack: book a 3BR with a formal dining room and ask host permission for small meetup. some hosts are cool if you promise not to be loud.
ben: cancellation policy is key. hotels often have nicer corporate cancellation windows. Airbnb host cancellations can be messy.
travis: pro tip: if we go Airbnbs, ask folks to use Instant Book or confirm within 24h. saves back-and-forth.
rachel: budget: finance prefers per-night per-person cap. Hotels may push that over for downtown. Thoughts?
priya: can we do hybrid — majority at a hotel, plus 1-2 nearby Airbnbs for folks who want roommates/smaller budgets?
jason: poll? :one: Hotel-only :two: Airbnb-only :three: Hybrid
ben: :one: from me — easier ops.
amanda: :three: — I vote for hybrid.
travis: :two: if we get a very cheap whole-house closeby.
